subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Mutual Inductance: Coils Talking to Coils
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mutual Inductance: Coils Talking to Coils.

hook.text: Two coils near each other share magnetic flux. Change current in one and voltage appears in the other.

buildup.text: The shared flux links them. More turns and closer spacing increase the coupling.

discovery.text: Mutual inductance M measures how much voltage one coil gets from current changes in another.

twist.text: Transformers maximize M on purpose. Wireless chargers rely on it too.

climax.text: Unwanted mutual inductance is called crosstalk — it corrupts signals on circuit boards.

punchline.text: Two coils, one changing field — energy transfers without wires.

quiz.question: What causes mutual inductance between two coils?
options: Electrostatic charge buildup between the coils
Changing current in one coil creates flux that links to the other
Physical vibration from one coil transfers to the other
